items.summary: Authored SB 14, designating human trafficking of a minor for a commercial sex act a serious felony under the Three Strikes law; it passed both houses unanimously with 64 legislative co-authors, was signed September 25, 2023, and took effect January 1, 2024; no measured outcome is recorded as of 2026-11-04.
items.title: SB 14 (2023): trafficking of a minor for a commercial sex act made a serious felony

citations.quote: The law designates human trafficking of a minor for purposes of a commercial sex act as a serious felony — including under the state’s “Three Strikes” law — and imposes harsher penalties and sentencing enhancements for individuals convicted of the crime.
SB 14, which passed the state Assembly and Senate unanimously, is a bipartisan measure co-authored by 64 members of the Legislature.
SB 14 goes into effect January 1, 2024.

items.summary: Authored SB 1414, raising the penalty for soliciting or purchasing a child for sex from a misdemeanor to a felony, with 16- and 17-year-olds required to be proven trafficking victims; signed by the Governor and effective January 1, 2025; no measured outcome is recorded as of 2026-11-04.
items.title: SB 1414 (2024): soliciting or purchasing a minor for sex made a felony

citations.quote: SB 1414 (Grove) increases the penalty for soliciting or purchasing a child for sex from a misdemeanor to a felony, with a caveat that 16 and 17-year-olds must be proven victims of human trafficking.
SB 1414 goes into effect January 1, 2025.

items.summary: Authored SB 373, the CAPE Act, requiring more frequent check-ins and face-to-face meetings between California school representatives and students placed in out-of-state nonpublic schools; signed by the Governor, effective January 1, 2026; no measured outcome is recorded as of 2026-11-04.
items.title: SB 373 (2025): Accountability for Placements in Education (CAPE) Act

citations.quote: SB 373 required more frequent check-ins and face-to-face meetings between California school representatives and vulnerable students sent out of state.
SB 373, also known as California’s Accountability for Placements in Education (CAPE) Act, was signed by Governor Gavin Newsom.
SB 373 will take effect on January 1, 2026.

items.summary: Authored SB 1190, the Safe Passage for Youth Act, requiring youth transportation companies to be permitted, employees to pass background checks, and banning middle-of-the-night pickups, blindfolds, hoods and unnecessary restraints; signed by the Governor, effective January 1, 2027.
items.title: SB 1190 (2026): Safe Passage for Youth Act

citations.quote: SB 1190 now requires youth transportation companies to be permitted, requires employees to pass background checks, and bans middle of the night pickups, blindfolds, hoods, and unnecessary restraints.
SB 1190, also known as the Safe Passage for Youth Act, was signed by Governor Gavin Newsom.
SB 1190 will take effect on January 1, 2027.

items.summary: Co-authored SB 931 with Senator John Laird, designating September 25 as Dolly Parton Day in California; signed by the Governor in 2026.
items.title: SB 931 (2026): September 25 designated Dolly Parton Day

citations.quote: Senator Shannon Grove (R-Bakersfield) and Senator John Laird (D-Santa Cruz) are proud to announce that their measure, Senate Bill 931, proclaiming 9-2-5, September 25 as Dolly Parton Day in California has been signed into law by Governor Newsom.
